2027-01-24.alt: Year B. Sunday of the Word of God, established by Pope Francis in 2019 (Aperuit illis). The memorial of St Francis de Sales is not kept this year because it falls on Sunday. Week of Prayer for Christian Unity. Liturgical colour: green.
2027-01-24.verse: Now after John was arrested, Jesus came to Galilee, proclaiming the good news of God, and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.”
theo: Mark's Gospel moves fast. John the Baptist is arrested, and Jesus begins at once: “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.” These are the first words of Jesus in Mark, a summary of all his preaching. The time of waiting is over; God's reign is here in person. Two responses are asked: repent, which means turn around and change your mind; and believe, which means trust and give yourself to the good news.

Then the call: Jesus sees Simon and Andrew casting their nets and says, “Follow me and I will make you fish for people.” “And immediately they left their nets and followed him.” James and John leave their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men. The word of Jesus is not information but a power that changes lives. Jonah's short sermon in Nineveh shows the same power: “the people of Nineveh believed God”, and God relented. Paul adds urgency: “the appointed time has grown short… the present form of this world is passing away.” We cannot hold this world's goods as if they were final.

Today is the Sunday of the Word of God. Pope Francis asked the whole Church to celebrate, study and spread the Scriptures on this day, recalling St Jerome: “Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.” The word that called the first disciples by the Sea of Galilee calls us through the Bible. Let us enthrone the Scriptures in our homes and read them daily.
conn: The Greek word is kairos, God's decisive moment, not ordinary clock time (chronos).

2027-01-24.prayer: Almighty ever-living God, direct our actions according to your good pleasure, that in the name of your beloved Son we may abound in good works. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, you call us as you called Simon and Andrew: give us hearts that repent and believe, hands that leave the nets that hold us, and a love for your word that reads it daily and lives it gladly. Amen.

illus: In a fishing village near Kollam, a parish began a custom on the Sunday of the Word of God: every family carries its Bible in procession to the altar for a blessing and takes it home to a place of honour. An old fisherman said: Jesus called fishermen first; it is right that fishermen should carry his word.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the first words of Jesus in Mark's Gospel are a summary of everything: the time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news (Mark 1:15). God's moment has arrived, and it arrives in the person of Jesus.

Two responses are asked. Repent: turn around, change your mind and heart. Believe: trust the good news and give yourself to it. Jonah's few words were enough for Nineveh: the people of Nineveh believed God (Jonah 3:5). How much more should the word of the Son move us.

Then Jesus walks by the sea and calls: follow me and I will make you fish for people. And immediately they left their nets and followed him (Mark 1:17–18). James and John even leave their father in the boat. The word of Jesus is not information; it is a power that changes life.
Paul adds urgency: the appointed time has grown short; the present form of this world is passing away (1 Corinthians 7:29, 31). We may use the things of this world, but we must not cling to them.

Today is the Sunday of the Word of God. Pope Francis asks every Catholic to love the Scriptures. St Jerome said that ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ. Let us give the Bible a place of honour in our homes, and read it every day.
The same Jesus who called the fishermen calls us now through his word. Let us leave our nets and follow him. Amen.

q: For surely I know the plans I have for you, says the LORD, plans for your welfare and not for harm, to give you a future with hope.
Now after John was arrested, Jesus came to Galilee, proclaiming the good news of God, and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.”
And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.

Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
